main_text.p: noxia, postremo res meliores quærunt & de his sibi prospiciunt, quæ sunt ad commodum & voluptates: Sic aqua, quæ incaluit, igne sublato, paulatim excutit calorem, & cudit sibi tacitis malleis, novum frigus: calor enim infestus Aquæ id agit, ut in fumum ac vapores resoluta difpereat, imo, quod horrendum est magis, dispareat, ne residuo quidem cadavere. Sed hic mihi jam, Pantomime, injicitur scrupulus, cur Aquæ frigus affectandum potius, quam calorem putes : ambo, cum modum excesserunt, ex æquo noxia sunt: calor eam in vapores, frigus in glaciem ver-

page.notes: The marginal notes on the right edge are show-through from the facing page and are not transcribed. The running head is reproduced as printed in small capitals. The word "ver-" at the foot is a line-end catchword-like hyphenated word continuing onto the next page; it is kept as printed. Some letters in the body are slightly faint (e.g. "horrendum", "resoluta") but read clearly.
